transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I keep forgetting things. Things I really shouldn't be forgetting. 

Like my heart follow-up appointments... or calling the clinic back. Even just showing up with the right tools for a repair job. It just... keeps slipping my mind, I suppose.
Did these memory problems start before you were 16 years old?

I suppose so. Yeah. 

Even back in grade school... I was the kid who couldn't really stay in his seat. Always blurting out answers. The teachers sent a lot of notes home to my folks about me talking too much. So... yes. It's been a long time.
Do these problems interfere with your daily life?

I suppose so. The... the guys at the senior-center repair group, they can't really count on me the way they used to. And... well, my doctor's office has been having to chase me down about those missed heart appointments. So... yeah. It gets in the way.
Have these memory problems gotten noticeably worse only in recent years?

Well... I suppose it has. It's really been causing trouble for... maybe a year and two months. 

I had a... a cardiac scare around then. The doctors told me I had to cut back on my walking. And my projects. Those things used to keep me settled, I think. So... yeah. It's been worse since I had to stop doing all that.
When you forget something, does a reminder usually bring it back to mind right away?
I suppose so. Yeah... if someone brings it up, I usually know what they're talking about. I just... I don't think of it on my own.
Have you noticed a clear worsening in your memory or concentration compared with how you were a few years ago?
I'm not really sure about a few years ago. Like I said... it's mostly just been since that heart thing last year. I haven't really kept track of it before then.
Have you noticed that these forgetfulness and concentration problems are new since the heart scare, or have they always been like this throughout your life?

Well... no, it's not exactly new. I mean... I've always been a bit like this, I guess. 

Even back when I was a boy in grade school... I was always the one who couldn't stay in his seat. I'd just blurt things out... get notes sent home because I talked too much. So... it's always been there. Just... more noticeable lately, I suppose.
Were you having trouble with attention, impulsivity, or restlessness before age 12?

Yeah... like I was just saying. Back in grade school. I was always that kid who couldn't stay in his chair... blurting out answers and getting those notes sent home for talking. So... yes. Well before I was twelve.
Compared with how you were before the heart scare, have your memory and concentration been getting worse overall?
I don't really know... hard to say, honestly. I haven't been keeping track of it like that. It's just... I notice it more now, I guess. I couldn't tell you if it's actually getting worse day by day.
Before your heart scare, were you able to manage your day-to-day tasks without these forgetfulness and concentration problems causing trouble?

I managed alright before, I guess. It's just... lately, it's getting in the way a bit more. 

Like with the repair group down at the senior center... they can't really count on me the way they used to. And... well, even my doctor's office has had to chase me down recently. Keep missing my heart follow-ups. So... yeah. It's causing some trouble.
Over the past year or so, have you noticed your memory getting progressively worse compared with how it was before?
I... I don't think so. I mean, it's not like a steady decline or anything. It's just... it's just what it is right now. I wouldn't say it's getting worse and worse over the year.
Have you noticed problems with memory or concentration in areas of life that were never an issue for you before?
I haven't really noticed anything like that. Just... well, just the things I already mentioned. Nothing new, I don't think.
Have you been having trouble learning or remembering new information, like recent conversations or instructions?
No, I... I wouldn't say so. Not really. Just... well, just the usual stuff. Nothing new like that.
Did these attention or memory problems first start after you turned 40?

No... long before that. Um... even back in grade school, I guess. I was always the kid who couldn't stay in his seat. I'd... blurt out answers. Got notes sent home for talking too much. So... yeah. It's just how I've always been.
Has your memory problem ever made you forget important things like appointments or bills even when you were using written reminders or a calendar?

Well... yeah, I suppose. That's... part of why I'm here. I just... keep forgetting things I shouldn't. Like my heart follow-up appointments. Or calling the clinic back. Even when I try to keep track, I'll still show up for a repair job without the right tools. It's... frustrating.
Have you noticed that your memory is clearly worse than it used to be?
No... I wouldn't say that. It's... pretty much the same as it's always been, I guess. Not... not worse. Just the same.
Have these memory and concentration problems clearly gotten worse compared with your usual level over the last few years?
No... I don't think so. Like I said... it's always been about the same. I haven't noticed it getting any worse lately.
Do you still have trouble paying attention to things you’re interested in, like reading a book or watching a movie?

I suppose so. Even with things I care about... it happens. Like if I sit down at the bridge table, or... a Fix-It Friends planning meeting. I mean to pay close attention. But after a little while, my mind just... slides off. Then I realize I missed half of what was said. So... yeah.
Have you ever gotten lost in a familiar place?
No... I haven't. I know my way around just fine.
Did you have these attention problems before age 12?

Yeah... I guess it goes back that far. Even back in grade school, I... well, I was the kid who couldn't stay in his seat. I'd, uh, blurt out answers a lot. My folks got a fair amount of notes sent home about me talking too much. So... yes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a longstanding childhood-onset attention/impulsivity syndrome consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive/hyperactive features, with symptoms present since grade school and before age 12. The patient reports chronic distractibility, forgetfulness, difficulty sustaining attention even for preferred activities, blurting out answers, excessive talking, and restlessness in childhood, with current functional impairment in daily responsibilities. Mild cognitive disorder is less likely because there is no evidence of new progressive cognitive decline, no clear worsening over recent years, and reminders usually restore recall.
